stories.headline: Russian strike on Ukrainian aid centre kills at least 26 after ceasefire ends

sources.body: Russia killed at least 26 people in strikes on a village in southern Ukraine on Monday, including civilians collecting humanitarian aid, emergency workers and police officers. The attack came hours after a rare ceasefire ended, extinguishing hopes of progress towards peace.
sources.headline: Russian strikes kill 26 in Ukraine after longest ceasefire ends

sources.body:
Ukrainian president Zelenskyy says attack on aid hub was ‘vile’ and shows Russia does not want to de-escalate

Russia on Monday bombed an aid distribution centre and neighbouring shelter in southern Ukraine , killing at least 26 ​people, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the country’s emergency services said.

Emergency services said two members of a rescue crew and four police officers were among the dead in the village ⁠of Komyshuvakha, in south-eastern Zaporizhzhia region. Five people were being treated in hospital, including two rescue workers.

Zelenskyy, in his nightly video address, said Russian forces initially dropped bombs on a school in the village that was used as a shelter and for ⁠distributing humanitarian assistance.

There were no classes at the school, he said, as the village, lying south-east of the region’s main city, ​also called Zaporizhzhia, was too close to the frontline. ‌

“The Russians struck first ‌just as people were arriving – a few aerial bombs,” he said. “Then there was a second strike – more air bombs, this time on ‌the shelter. A vile terrorist strike.”

As night fell in Komyshuvakha, emergency responders used torches to search through the rubble of collapsed buildings, according to photos and video posted online by local officials. Regina Kharchenko, secretary of the Zaporizhzhia city council, said that 27 people were missing in the attack.

Efforts to rescue people Monday evening were hindered as Russian drones launched additional attacks in the area that had been bombed, according to Mykhailo Semikin, a military official in Zaporizhzhia.

Zelenskyy said the Russians could not have been unaware that residents remaining in Komyshuvakha gathered each week to pick up humanitarian packages from the site.

The attack, he said, had shown that Moscow was intent on killing people instead of building on the past week’s ceasefire in the embattled southern city of Oleshky , brokered by US first lady Melania Trump.

“Russians continue to demonstrate, time and again, their hatred of Ukraine and everything that exists here,” he said.

“If Russia genuinely ‌wanted de-escalation, there was an opportunity following the situation in Oleshky to continue taking humanitarian steps. We proposed this. But Russia continues to kill people.”

The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied Oleshky.

It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, now in its fifth year, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned “at the moment”.

US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume next week, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.

President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but there has been no breakthrough.

The talks – to be held 10 November and 11 in Abu Dhabi, Witkoff said – come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.

*With Reuters, Associated Press and Agence France-Presse
sources.headline: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills at least 26, Kyiv says

stories.headline: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as talks continue over the Strait of Hormuz

sources.body: The United States reportedly struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, even as President Donald Trump signalled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The reported attack was the latest in a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out in recent weeks.
sources.headline: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Trump signals progress in talks

sources.body:
Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions on the island in the strait of Hormuz, coming on the eve of crucial US midterms

The ⁠US launched limited strikes on ​Iran’s Qeshm Island late on Monday, ⁠according to reports in US media, hours after US vice-president JD Vance said he was optimistic diplomatic efforts to end the war were moving in the right direction.

The strikes were reported as being “defensive”, and not thought to be a signal of a return to full hostilities, but came on the eve of crucial midterm elections in which Donald Trump’s Republican party is expected to be punished by voters for the cascading effect the war has had on the US cost of living.

When asked earlier on Monday whether he had considered resuming strikes on Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections, Trump replied “no”.

Several explosions were ⁠heard ⁠on Qeshm ​Island on Monday evening, according to Iranian state media, with local outlets describing their cause as unclear. The strikes – first reported by the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) – targeted surface to air missiles being used against US assets, according to Reuters and the Associated Press.

US Central ‌Command did ​not immediately ⁠respond to ​a request for ​comment from the Reuters news agency, and the WSJ described the attacks as part of a series of strikes carried out against the country in recent weeks that have not been made public.

The paper said that sources suggested the recent strikes have been carried out on a smaller scale and purposefully kept secret by the Trump administration so as not to signal ‌any intent of resuming the military campaign against Iran.

The US has targeted Qeshm Island on multiple occasions throughout the war. Positioned in the mouth of the strait of Hormuz, the island has been used in the past to launch attacks on shipping in the waterway.

Despite attacks having ceased in recent weeks, Iran has continued to enforce its closure of the strait by targeting oil tankers, shipping containers and other vessels attempting to transit the waterway.

If confirmed, the attack would mark the first publicly known strike by the US on Iran in weeks . On Monday Vance said that he and Trump were optimistic about securing a deal with Iran , after Tehran revealed indirect negotiations with Washington.

“The president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement,” Vance told reporters. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more.”

Speaking to Fox News hours before the polls opened in the US on Tuesday, Trump continued to play down the significance of the conflict and its effects on the US economy.

“There’s no war raging. It could happen if they don’t make a deal, but they want to make a deal very badly and there’s a very good chance we make a deal.”

Speaking from Washington in his closing message of the midterms campaign, Trump hailed a sharp drop in oil prices that came as his administration touted a renewed diplomatic efforts being made to end the war. Rising petrol prices have caused by the war have become a signature issue of the midterm elections, with polls showing voters likely to punish Republicans for the effect on the cost of living.
sources.headline: US reportedly strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island as Vance voices optimism about a deal

stories.headline: European troops to rehearse a possible post-ceasefire deployment to Ukraine

sources.body: Around 2,800 troops from 10 European countries will take part in a military exercise in southeastern Poland from November 9 to 22, testing a multinational force designed to support Ukraine after a potential ceasefire. Led by France and Britain, the force aims to bolster Ukraine's security without taking on an offensive role.
sources.headline: European force to hold first Ukraine support exercise in Poland

sources.body:
Britain and France are to lead a military exercise to test a multinational force's ability to deploy to Ukraine, if there is a peace deal.

Nearly 3,000 military personnel from 12 European nations will take part in the rehearsal in neighbouring Poland this month.

Plans for a reassurance force for Ukraine were set out last year as one of the long-term security guarantees being proposed by European nations.

But there are still more questions than answers as to how such a military force might work in practice. Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in offensive operations or be involved in peacekeeping or ceasefire monitoring missions.

Nor would they be operating under the command of Nato or on the front line.

Officials say their presence would be to provide reassurance to Ukraine and to help rebuild its armed forces.

The US has been involved in discussions, but is not contributing to the mission.

Russia has already voiced opposition to foreign troops being stationed in Ukraine and, last year, President Vladimir Putin said they would be "legitimate targets".

Western officials have declined to spell out the rules of engagement if any international troops were to be attacked in Ukraine. Though they say the force would be able to defend itself.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the exercise showed Britain, France and their allies were stepping up preparation for the day when peace came to Ukraine.

He said: "This is not a hypothetical plan, it's a real force, ready to help Ukraine once the fighting stops."

Lt Gen Tom Bateman, the UK commander of the Multi National Force – Ukraine (MNF-U), said the exercise represented an important step in translating political commitments into credible military readiness.

He said it was a "real, capable, readily deployable force that represented a serious commitment from Coalition of the Willing nations to Ukraine's long-term stability and security".

Exercise Koalicja - which takes place from 9-22 November - will be a rehearsal of how to move, protect and supply a force in Ukraine. It will also be a test of their command and control to ensure troops from different countries can work together.

Some 2,800 military personnel will take part across land, sea and air, with the UK contribution including 300 troops and a pair of RAF Typhoons.

Fighter jets will simulate how they would reassure commercial aircraft once Ukraine's skies can be reopened.

Turkey has agreed to lead the maritime mission, with the eventual goal to clear mines and allow the resumption of trade in the Black Sea.

As well as the UK, troops will come from France, Belgium, Estonia, France, Germany, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Sweden, and Turkey.

However, Western officials could not comment on the final make-up and shape of the force that could be deployed to Ukraine if the fighting stops.

In the past, military experts have suggested that Western nations might have to send tens of thousands of troops to Ukraine to guarantee its security.
sources.headline: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace

stories.headline: Cyberattack disrupts supermarket refrigeration across Europe

sources.body:
Chains in seven countries say cooling unit temperatures rose overnight in incident similar to hack of French shops

Who is hacking Europe’s supermarket fridges and freezers, and why?

Supermarket chains in at least seven European countries have said the temperatures of refrigerators and freezers in some of their shops soared overnight to as high as 50C (122F), echoing a cyber-attack last month that caused millions of euros of damage in France.

Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Finland, Luxembourg , the Netherlands and Sweden reported problems with their refrigeration systems on Monday, and several companies confirmed they had been hacked.

The EU food and agriculture commissioner, Christophe Hansen, said the repeated cyber-attacks were deeply concerning, calling them “a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers’ confidence in it”.

The incidents follow an attack in France last month in which hackers seized control of cooling units in as many as 700 supermarkets, raising their temperatures as high ⁠as 50C (122F) and causing fires and food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros.

A growing range of devices, including refrigeration systems, can now be monitored and controlled remotely, leading authorities to particularly fear government-sponsored hybrid attacks ​in after Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Sweden’s Coop chain told the daily Aftonbladet that six of ​its shops ‌had been ​hit, while ICA said it was “aware that a limited ​number of stores were affected by an incident overnight which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems”.

An ICA shop at Sjöbo in southern Sweden posted that its fridges and freezers had been hacked and their temperature set at 50C. Another in Stockholm said its freezers were broken “due to a 2am cyberattack” and that “everything was destroyed”.

The head of Sweden’s national cybersecurity centre, John Billow, said it ‌was working on incidents around the country. It had established the country had “quite a lot of exposed operational ‌technology devices” that needed updating or patching, he told Reuters.

The Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize, which last ​month ​reported a ​similar incident ​to police in the Netherlands, said fridges and ⁠freezers in dozens of its ⁠supermarkets in ​Belgium ‌and ‌Luxembourg had been hit.

It did not specify the cause, but reporters visiting a shop north-east of Brussels saw refrigerators and freezers empty and a sign reading: “Due to cyberattacks, there will be no products on the refrigerated or freezer shelves. We offer our sincere apologies.”

A company spokesperson, Sarah ‌De Meester, said the range of fresh and frozen products was “temporarily somewhat limited” in affected shops, but that distribution centres were operating normally and there was no disruption to deliveries.

Belgium’s Le Soir newspaper reported that dozens of shops and supermarkets had been affected, including five Spar outlets, Shop & Go convenience shops attached to Q8 service stations and some smaller Proxy Delhaize mini-markets.
sources.headline: Shop fridges and freezers across Europe hit by fresh suspected cyber-attack

sources.body: Grocery stores from Sweden to Portugal were hit Monday by a suspected cyberattack on their freezer systems, in what the EU denounced as a deliberate attempt to disrupt the bloc's food chain. Supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg and the Netherlands were among at least eight countries affected in the incident, which came three weeks after a cyberattack caused mass disruption in French grocery stores. Food retailers were forced to throw out produce that had spoiled or was at risk of spoiling after refrigerator temperatures soared overnight. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
sources.headline: EU says fridge attacks 'deliberate attempt to disrupt' bloc's food supply

stories.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has killed more than 5,300 people

sources.body:
The current Bundibugyo strain has spread to Kenya and Uganda, while two in Nigeria returned negative results.

The death toll from the latest Ebola outbreak in Africa has surpassed 5,300, with the majority of cases recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC).

The DRC is the epicentre of the latest outbreak, having declared its 17th – and largest – Ebola outbreak in mid-May.

According to data from the Africa CDC on Monday, the outbreak has killed 5,376 people: 5,372 in the DRC and two each in Kenya and Uganda.

The Bundibugyo strain of the virus, responsible for the current outbreak, has infected some 10,444 people in the DRC, Uganda and Kenya, with a death rate of more than 50 percent.

The virus has crossed borders several times in recent months.

Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 cases, almost all involving people who had travelled from the DRC, before being declared Ebola-free in August.

Kenya recorded two deaths and nine infections in October, marking the first recorded cases of Ebola in the country.

In Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, health authorities said two rounds of testing of two suspected cases in the northeast region confirmed the samples were negative.

Abuja reported its first imported case in October, the first in more than a decade. It has no recorded deaths.

In France, a single case involving a health worker returning from the DRC was reported in July.

There are no approved treatments or vaccines to combat the rare Bundibugyo strain.

In recent weeks, clinical trials have begun with the Ervebo vaccine, which has proved effective against the more common Zaire strain.
sources.headline: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people in DR Congo

stories.headline: Australia’s high court hears challenge to ban on social media for under-16s

sources.body:
Reddit challenges ban on grounds it impinges implied freedom of political communications for teens

The Australian government’s rush to pass the under-16s social media ban legislation in 2024 led to “ill-thought-out, over-broad legislation” that has since been narrowed after Reddit sued the government, lawyers for the social media company told the high court on Tuesday.

Reddit, one of the top 10 websites visited in the world, has challenged the teen social media ban on the grounds that it impinges the implied freedom of political communication for under-16s.

In oral arguments before the high court on Tuesday, Reddit’s counsel, Perry Herzfeld SC, argued in the years leading up to the ban legislation, a 2021 parliamentary inquiry on social media had not recommended introducing a ban, with the eSafety commissioner warning the inquiry at the time it would be a “blunt force approach”.

When the government announced the ban in 2024, Reddit argued the legislation was introduced and passed within a week, with only 24 hours of submissions allowed.

“A process of this kind is likely to lead to ill-thought-out, over-broad legislation,” Herzfeld argued.

After eSafety announced Reddit would be included in the ban , and Reddit did not accept it met the definition of a social media platform under the law, the company announced the high court challenge to the law in late 2025.

In March this year, the communications minister, Anika Wells, introduced new rules as part of the legislation that defines additional requirements for social media companies to meet the definition including logged-in features, recommendation features, or endless scroll.

Herzfeld argued that the ban does not address those factors specifically by a broad ban on under-16s accounts, and has argued it would be able to under different legislation – pointing to the digital duty of care legislation currently before the parliament.

Outside the court, Wells told reporters that she wasn’t the minister at the time the legislation passed, but said the government’s arguments in response would be made in court.

Since the ban came into effect in December last year, more than 5 million user accounts across 10 platforms that those platforms believe to belong to people aged under 16 have been suspended or deactivated.

The platforms covered by the ban currently include Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, Kick, X, Twitch and Threads.

The case centres around whether the effect of the ban limiting political communications is justified by what the government has said is a “credible risk” of harms such as mental health issues, sleeping issues, and eating disorder issues among others.

Herzfeld told the court on Tuesday the burden on teens of the ban is limitations to actively engage in political communications through subreddits such as r/Australia. While they can still view the content without an account, they can’t make their own posts, comment, or upvote content, Reddit argued.

Justice Jacqueline Gleeson expressed reservations when pointed to examples of high-profile teens being politically engaged in social media – such as 6News’ Leo Puglisi , who began his news site at the age of 11.
sources.headline: Australia rushed through ‘ill-thought-out’ under-16s social media ban, Reddit argues as high court challenge begins

sources.body:
Two days of hearings on a challenge to Australia's landmark social media ban for children will begin at the country's highest court on Tuesday.

In a major test of the world-leading policy, a digital rights group will argue that the ban for under-16s robs children of their right to free communication. A separate challenge launched by platform Reddit will be jointly heard.

Introduced last December, the ban is a key part of sweeping changes the Australian government has spearheaded in recent years on online safety.

Supporters say the ban protects children from harmful content but critics say it is too blunt an instrument and efforts should focus on improving online safety.

The constitutional challenge in Australia's High Court was filed by the Digital Freedom Project a few weeks before the ban started on 10 December last year. The group is lead by New South Wales parliamentarian John Ruddick.

Two teens who originally spearheaded the case , Noah Jones and Macy Neyland, have since withdrawn as plaintiffs though Jones is still expected to attend Tuesday's hearing.

Speaking about the legal challenge last November, Jones told the BBC that there were bad things online but a blanket ban for under-16s was not the right answer.

"We shouldn't be using the resources and money of these social media platforms to try to avoid fines from our government," he said.

"They should be using this money and resources to try to get rid of the predators and harmful content out there."

Reddit also launched a High Court challenge to the ban, arguing the policy has serious implications for privacy and political rights.

The company said it shared Australia's goal of protecting young people online "but there are better and more effective ways" than a ban.

"As we challenge this law in court, we'll continue to comply with it and advocate for more effective youth safety measures," said Reddit's chief communications officer Adam Collins.

Communications Minister Anika Wells last year said the government would not be "intimidated by legal threats."

"We will not be intimidated by big tech. On behalf of Australian parents, we will stand firm," she said last November.

Under the ban, ten platforms - Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Snapchat, X, Kick, Threads and Twitch - must take "reasonable steps" to ensure no one under 16 years old can access its site.

Platforms risk fines of up to A$99m (US$70m, £52m) for serious or repeated breaches, but since the ban started, no company has been fined.

The eSafety Commissioner - the body tasked with enforcing the ban - has launched several investigations into alleged non-compliance by Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube.

WhatsApp and online gaming sites like Roblox and Discord were not included in the ban, nor were educational platforms like YouTube Kids and Google Classroom.

In the first few days of the ban, Meta - which owns three of the banned platforms - said it had closed about half a million accounts.

Some children said they were booted off their accounts in the days before and when the ban started - but many have said they were able to easily circumvent the age checks which included uploading credit card details, photo IDs or a selfie.
sources.headline: Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court

sources.body: Americans head to the polls on Tuesday for the US midterm elections, which could flip the majority in one or both houses of Congress from the Republicans to the Democrats. What would a Democratic majority mean for the country's political landscape, and how might Democrats move to keep President Donald Trump in check?

stories.headline: Republicans privately blame Trump as they brace for midterm losses

sources.body: Republicans are already privately blaming President Donald Trump as they brace for losses on Tuesday. Even as they race to distance themselves from his actions on tariffs, the unpopular Iran war and his mass deportation agenda, few have been willing to criticize him publicly — a clear sign of just how powerful Trump's grip remains on the GOP. But interviews with roughly a dozen candidates, campaign officials and lawmakers reveal they're acutely aware of who, exactly, put them on the back foot this entire cycle. "There was a point earlier this year where we really felt like we could defy history," said one House Republican, who, like others in this article, was granted anonymity to candidly discuss midterms dynamics. "And then Trump bombed Iran. And it was just one thing after another.” Republicans are tied or trailing in polls in numerous critical battlegrounds and expecting to lose some once-secure red seats. And Trump's unfocused closing message — including repeated comments about male candidates' physical appearances — has further frustrated an already on-edge party. “I think Jon Husted's ass and Nicki Minaj's is a great closing message,” T.W. Arrighi, a Republican strategist working on the South Carolina Senate race and others, said sarcastically in an interview on The Conversation with Dasha Burns . “You’ve got to take the good with the bad with Trump, unless you want to drive yourself crazy every day.” “People are gonna go after the president. The buck stops with him. His approval ratings aren't great,” he added. Privately, some Republicans are even harsher. “At least when Barack Obama was president, he only screwed his enemies, never his friends,” said a second House Republican. The White House defended its involvement in the war with Iran, tariff regime and approach to immigration enforcement. Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement that Trump “is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress.” One White House official, granted anonymity to speak candidly, called the blame game “an asinine adventure” and said Trump “has obviously left it all on the field.” If the bottom falls out for the GOP on Tuesday, the quiet calls assigning him blame may turn into a public shanking as Trump nears the lame-duck stage of his presidency, Republicans refocus on how to win voters back for 2028 and jostle for their own spots in the party’s future. “I'm not sure what the Republican Party looks like in six months. Look, a lot of Republicans have held their tongues. A lot of Republicans who have real problems with the way things have gone the last two years have been good soldiers,” said a Republican strategist involved in competitive midterm races across the country. “But what happens if we lose 35 House seats and six Senate seats?” “We all know who the problem is. It’s Trump. And do we continue down a path of losing?” the strategist added. In Georgia, some Republicans have already warned that low early voting turnout in rural parts of the state could drag down their entire ticket. "If you live in rural Georgia, you're going to be disproportionately hurt by higher — especially diesel — prices,” said Jason Shepherd, the former GOP chair of suburban Cobb County. “The promise of the great Trump economy has not materialized." Top Hill Republicans have worked behind the scenes for months to try to alleviate some of the political fallout from Trump’s election year policy moves, including arguing to White House officials that Maine Sen. Susan Collins and Michigan Senate nominee Mike Rogers could lose their races if the administration didn’t reach an off-ramp from the trade war with Canada, according to three Republicans with direct knowledge of the matter. Eventually, Trump agreed to roll back some tariffs and add new ones in a boost to Collins. Republicans also pressed for the White House to undo some of Trump’s other controversial moves, like his executive order to import more foreign beef that has riled ranchers and farmers in red states like Kansas, Iowa and Texas. But that relief never came. "Republicans have always been aware of the historical midterm precedent, and that's why we're barnstorming the country to tout the president's achievements on cutting taxes, securing the border, and lowering drug costs,” said Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee. “Any anonymous strategist who says the president is not helpful in turning out Republican voters has no idea what they're talking about, and their candidates should request a refund for their shoddy consulting services." But Trump’s actions, Republicans say, are hitting different parts of the country hard. The Iran war, they argue, was a significant blunder from Trump that has multiplied Democrats’ paths to power in both the House and Senate by driving fuel and fertilizer costs up — most notably impacting races across the Midwest. The White House’s tariffs regime has been a major concern in battlegrounds on the Canadian border like Maine and Michigan. Hardline immigration enforcement that has resulted in the deportation of thousands has hurt especially in heavily Latino border states like Arizona and Texas, and the cancelling of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Venezuelans has enraged South Florida voters. Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar, a Miami Republican, warned the president in a campaign ad earlier this year that his immigration tactics had gone too far. “Trump won Miami, and yet he went to the place that gave him the biggest support, and kind of just fucked everybody over if we're being honest.” said one Florida-based Republican operative. New results from The POLITICO Poll show that Republican midterm voters are split over who they would blame if the GOP performs worse than it did in 2024: A sizable 29% blame Trump for making the GOP less popular, while 30% said it is because Trump himself is not on the ballot. Fourteen percent said it would be because the Democratic Party has become more popular, while roughly one in four said they don’t know. Some in the party question whether Trump’s last-minute campaign travel across the country and the millions of dollars his political operation has poured into battleground states will even be enough. They see him as more absorbed in protecting his legacy than making actionable policy changes to help his party stay in power. “He cares more about the ballroom than he cares about Republicans winning the midterms,” said a third Republican strategist working in battleground races. “He wants the Nobel Peace Prize, these big legacy-defining things seem to be taking up more of his attention than actually being president.” A fourth GOP operative working on midterms races has a curt message if Republicans lose big: “Thank you, Donald Trump." Dasha Burns contributed reporting.
sources.headline: ‘A lot of Republicans have held their tongues’: Anger at Trump is growing

stories.headline: Midterms put Republican redistricting in Texas and elsewhere to the test

sources.body:
Partisan redistricting has transformed election for Black voters in Houston as Democrats seek new pathways to victory.

Houston, Texas – The gospel music from Mount Hebron Missionary Baptist Church spills into the streets of Sunnyside, a predominantly Black neighbourhood in southern Houston.

It is a familiar scene on any given Sunday: hands in the air, immaculate bow ties on starched shirts, fabric flowers adorning perfectly pastel hats. But with the US midterm elections just two days away, the service held a special significance on the front line of a US redistricting battle .

Mt Hebron had long been located in the ninth congressional district, its politically engaged Black voters for two decades helping to elect Democrat Al Green, a flamboyant presence in Congress known for his cane-waving opposition to US President Donald Trump.

But following an appeal from Trump, the Republican state legislature last year conducted rare mid-decade redistricting, redrawing the church and its Black community into the Black-majority 18th district.

Critics call the process “cracking and packing”, diminishing the representation in Congress of minority groups, particularly heavily Democratic Black communities, by consolidating their voting power into fewer districts.

“It’s kind of one and the same when we talk about the voting and the civil rights,” said Pastor Max Miller, who has served at the church for 18 years.

“They are trying to manipulate and monopolise the vote and minimise the people who are in those districts,” said Miller. “We see so much rolling backwards that it looks like they’re trying to take a script from an old song and turn back the hands of time.”

As a result of the redistricting, Green was forced to run in a primary against 18th district incumbent Christian Menefee, another Black Democrat. He lost, and Houston lost one of its Black representatives in Congress.

The ninth district, meanwhile, was redrawn to favour Republicans, one of at least five US congressional seats the party hopes to pick up in the midterm vote.

The machinations have resonated with worshippers at Mt Hebron.

“I don’t like the redistricting at all because Al Green was moved out,” said 97-year-old Alice Jefferson, who had followed the congressman throughout his political career. “He always had good advice for the people.”

Janice Ray, a 61-year-old home health aide and entrepreneur, said state lawmakers were “trying to move people out of the district that they’re familiar with”.

“To me, it was all a bunch of BS,” she said. “There was no reason for it.”

“But we’ll stand firm, regardless of what they try to do,” Ray added. “Because just like it was changed, it can always be changed back.”

The redistricting process has undergone a generational transformation this election season, one that, experts say, has degraded longstanding guardrails protecting minority voting power.

“In political science, we have what we call descriptive representation,” Michael Adams, a professor at Texas Southern University in Houston, told Al Jazeera. “In terms of descriptive representation, minorities and others feel that if they can elect someone who reflects their values, for example, and who may look like them, their voting can be defined as one voice.”
sources.headline: US midterms present a test for Republican redistricting in Texas and beyond

sources.body: <p>La Guardia Civil ya ha interrogado a una veintena de personas por el accidente ferroviario del pasado miércoles en Urda (Toledo) en el que murieron 69 personas, según detallan fuentes cercanas a la investigación. stories.headline: Barcelona plans to complete Diagonal tram connection in early 2031

sources.body: El tramvia ja ho té a tocar: durant el primer trimestre del 2031 el Trambaix i el Trambesòs quedaran completament connectats per la Diagonal , de punta a punta. Aquesta setmana, l’Ajuntament obrirà el concurs per trobar les empreses que facin les obres al tram de 2,8 km que queda ara encara sense vies, entre Verdaguer i Francesc Macià. Les obres començaran a l’estiu , tal com va anunciar l’alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni. A diferència del que es va plantejar fa uns mesos, la transformació d’aquests quasi 3 km es farà tota de cop i no per fases , i al llarg d’aquest recorregut del tramvia es crearan tres parades: Diagonal – Cinc d’Oros , Balmes i Casanova . Les obres que surten a concurs inclouen els projectes de la infraestructura tramviària, els de la reurbanització de la superfície i els d’ampliació (o desdoblament, en funció del tram) del col·lector d’aigües pluvials que hi ha sota terra. També et pot interessar Barcelona posa a prova un model experimental del col·lector de la Diagonal a escala reduïda Marc Bermejo Maria Solans 2 minuts de lectura Tot i que l’entrada en funcionament del tramvia serà el primer trimestre del 2031, les obres hauran acabat una mica abans (a finals del 2030). Hi caldrà sumar uns quatre mesos més per completar les proves i les marxes en blanc , abans que el servei sigui cent per cent operatiu. Com quedarà la Diagonal amb el tramvia? La implantació del tramvia comportarà la transformació de la Diagonal, tal com ja ha passat —evidentment— als trossos d’avinguda que ja tenen TRAM. Ara bé, aquesta transformació de la superfície no serà igual al llarg dels 2,8 km. Entre el passeig de Sant Joan i el passeig de Gràcia : la reurbanització de la Diagonal serà exactament la mateixa que té ara al tram entre Glòries i el passeig de Sant Joan. Això significa que l’avinguda es renovarà tota , de façana a façana, per fer les voreres més amples, dos carrils per a cotxes a cada banda i, al tronc central, el tramvia i el carril bici. Entre el passeig de Gràcia i Francesc Macià : aquí l’obra serà menys complicada perquè s’aprofitarà la reforma que es va fer el 2015 . La diferència amb l’estat actual és que el trànsit desapareixerà del tronc central perquè hi anirà el TRAM i també el carril bici. Com que les bicis sortiran dels laterals, hi cabrà un carril més per a cotxes a banda i banda. Entre el passeig de Gràcia i la via Augusta, el tramvia i el bus compartiran plataforma . 12.500 viatges menys en cotxe Completar la connexió dels tramvies a través de la Diagonal suposarà un paradigma en la mobilitat horitzontal de la ciutat. Segons càlculs de l’Ajuntament, la demanda de passatgers que s’espera per al nou TRAM de punt a punta és de 75 milions de persones cada any , el doble de volum que té ara. I també hi haurà una reducció de la mobilitat en cotxe: cada dia feiner es faran uns 12.500 trajectes menys en vehicle privat , segons la previsió municipal. Tot i això, la culminació del tramvia connectat obligarà a reordenar com conviuen les vies amb els cotxes i els busos interurbans a l’avinguda (més enllà de Francesc Macià, en direcció a Esplugues) i a la mateixa plaça de Francesc Macià. Aquí, el tramvia vorejarà la plaça pel cantó mar, tal com ja passa ara a l’encreuament de la Diagonal amb el passeig de Sant Joan. També et pot interessar D’on prové la dita “Donar més voltes que el 29”? Redacció programes 3 minuts de lectura

sources.body:
Un tranvía se desplaza por el paseo de Sant Joan. / Ajuntament de Barcelona

Todo apunta a que la conexión del tranvía por la Diagonal entrará en servicio durante el primer trimestre de 2031 . El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona y la Autoritat del Transport Metropolità (ATM) han dado el paso definitivo para su contratación y esta semana la empresa municipal BIMSA lanzará el proceso de licitación de los trabajos que durarán 40 meses con un presupuesto de 120 millones de euros con IVA.

Se trata de la segunda fase de la conexión tranviaria , entre Verdaguer y Francesc Macià, un trayecto de 2.800 metros y con tres paradas nuevas -Diagonal | Cinc d’Oros, Balmes y Casanova- que permitirá cruzar la avenida en unos 40 minutos de punta a punta , con la previsión de que aumente la demanda hasta los 75 millones de viajes anuales y que se reduzcan 12.500 desplazamientos en vehículo privado en los días laborables.

En cifras, la intervención abarca una superficie de 115.000 metros cuadrados . Se incrementará en 16.000 metros cuadrados el espacio peatonal, se ganarán 18.900 metros cuadrados de zonas verdes y se destinarán un total de 8.700 metros cuadrados, 1.800 más que actualmente, al espacio ciclista, con un carril bici bidireccional de 4 metros de ancho.

Entre las actuaciones menos visibles, pero quizá más importantes, se encuentra la ampliación y el desdoblamiento del colector , que reducirá el riesgo de inundaciones y de acumulación de agua en la superficie de la avenida y su entorno, con un incremento de hasta el 60% de la capacidad hidráulica . Una obra muy relevante en el actual contexto de emergencia climática y que dará continuidad a la actuación realizada en la primera fase de las obras de conexión del tranvía.

Las obras se dividirán en cinco lotes diferenciados y se ejecutarán todos a la vez, pero no será necesario cortar el tráfico ni el carril bici , que se mantendrá junto a los dos carriles por sentido compartidos entre el coche y el transporte público.

Los tres primeros lotes incluirán la obra de ampliación del colector ubicado en el subsuelo de la Diagonal , la infraestructura tranviaria bajo rasante y la reurbanización en los tres tramos definidos entre el paseo de Sant Joan y la avenida de Sarrià. El cuarto estará destinado a la plataforma tranviaria y las paradas de todo el tramo entre Verdaguer y la avenida de Sarrià, mientras que el quinto se centrará en las instalaciones de energía necesarias para alimentar todo el tramo, así como la red tranviaria unificada.

Si todo va según lo previsto, las obras se adjudicarán en primavera y los contratos se formalizarán con las empresas adjudicatarias para que los trabajos puedan comenzar el próximo verano. El objetivo es completar las obras en 40 meses, a los que habrá que sumar el periodo de pruebas previo a la puesta en servicio del tranvía, un calendario que supone una reducción significativa respecto al tiempo que habría requerido el anterior modelo de ejecución no simultáneo.

Más allá de la llegada del tranvía, el proyecto también transformará la configuración de una de las avenidas más emblemáticas de Barcelona, aunque los cambios serán diferentes en función del tramo.

stories.headline: Catalan leaders oppose a possible closure of the Barcelona–Madrid high-speed line

El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, aseguró en su segunda rueda de prensa tras el accidente ferroviario de Toledo que estaba sopesando, junto a sus colaboradores, la posibilidad de cambiar la forma de trabajar ante las obras que se llevan a cabo en las infraestructuras, como las de la alta velocidad. En España se opta por mantener el servicio, aunque comporte afectaciones para los usuarios, en lugar de cortarlo por completo hasta su finalización, pero ante las próximas obras que sufrirá el servicio de AVE entre Madrid y Barcelona , el president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa, prefiere mantener el modelo imperante, no en vano, Catalunya sufre desde hace años las obras de adecuación de Rodalies con la máxima de mantener el servicio de la red mientras sea posible.

En una entrevista en la Cadena Ser, Illa ha indicado que él es partidario de mantener esta línea de actuación, que hasta ahora se ha llevado a cabo en nuestro país, a diferencia de en otros lugares como Alemania, donde se opta por decisiones más drásticas en pro de la seguridad. “Si se puede mantener la seguridad, es la opción preferible. Creo que es lo deseable por parte de todos”, ha opinado el president.

El debate en cuestión se suscita por el hecho de que está previsto que las obras de remodelación integral de la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Zaragoza-Barcelona comiencen a finales de este año o a principios del 2027, unas obras cuyos trabajos prioritarios se concentran en el tramo entre Madrid y Calatayud.

Ante la situación generada por el nuevo accidente ferroviario, Illa ha apostado por la “renovación, cuando proceda, de todas las infraestructuras”, pero “con criterios de máxima seguridad y afectando lo mínimo posible el servicio”. “Soy partidario de mantener esta línea”, y el ministro Puente “hizo la reflexión de cómo se hace en otros lugares”, ha relegado.

Pero el president no se ha querido mojar sobre la posible dimisión del ministro y se ha limitado a indicar que el titular de Transportes “lo que tiene que hacer es lo que está haciendo: atender a sus responsabilidades dando explicaciones como lo está haciendo”. En este sentido, Illa ha recordado las palabras del presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, cuando dijo que “no es asumible” tener un nuevo accidente ferroviario en tan poco tiempo, por eso ha apostado por “analizar caso a caso lo que ha ocurrido y ver qué se puede hacer para mejorar la seguridad atendiendo a lo que dicen los expertos”.

En materia ferroviaria, Transportes y la Generalitat tienen pendiente el traspaso de la línea R1 de Rodalies, que debería llevarse a cabo antes de las elecciones del 29-N pero que podría sufrir alguna variación por lo sucedido en Urda. Illa ha rechazado cualquier alteración sobre los planes previstos al señalar que “las prioridades y objetivos son los mismos” y “lo ocurrido no afecta al esquema de trabajo” previsto.

El hecho de que este accidente haya impactado de lleno en el periodo electoral, con una pugna abierta entre PSOE y PP-Vox, ha generado un desánimo en la izquierda que Illa no parece estar dispuesto a aceptar. El president ha mostrado su “confianza” en que a pesar del grave accidente, los ciudadanos “saben distinguir el grano de la paja y los criterios sobre los que deben elegir”.
sources.headline: Illa apuesta por mantener el AVE Madrid-Barcelona aunque haya obras

sources.body: Amb l’accident ferroviari de Toledo encara molt recent, el ministre de Transports, Óscar Puente, va posar sobre la taula divendres passat la possibilitat de tancar la línia d’alta velocitat Barcelona-Madrid temporalment per renovar la infraestructura . Un anunci que ha sacsejat el sector ferroviari i que ha fet saltar les alarmes. En una entrevista al programa bàsics , de betevé, el director del Centre d’Estudis del Transport, Joan Carles Salmerón , ha afirmat que és una opció “ totalment inviable “. L’expert ha assegurat que la línia dona servei cada dia a entre 40.000 i 50.000 passatgers, una quantitat d’usuaris que no es pot absorbir “ni amb un pont aeri reforçat o carreteres reforçades”. Salmerón també ho ha descrit com un “ error de comunicació anunciar el tall poques hores després d’un accident”. “Són unes obres que es fan per renovar al complet una via després de 20 anys d’ús, no és per una manca de seguretat “, ha afegit. Tampoc no veu amb bons ulls l’explicació que el ministre de Transports va fer sobre les caigudes del sistema de seguretat LZB , quan va assegurar que durant el 2026 havia caigut 170 vegades. “No va aclarir si eren caigudes de menys d’un segon o si eren grans caigudes com la que va causar l’accident d’Urda. Hauria de donar més explicacions de manera immediata “, ha afirmat. També et pot interessar El Govern espanyol estudia aturar l’alta velocitat Madrid-Barcelona per fer-hi obres de millora Andrea Muñoz 3 minuts de lectura Un model alemany que no es pot aplicar a Espanya Aturar una línia ferroviària per fer-hi tasques de renovació és una pràctica molt habitual en altres països, com Alemaya. Salmerón, però, ha explicat que és complicat poder realitzar aquest tall a Espanya. “ Alemanya conserva totes les línies convencionals, però aquí gairebé no es poden fer servir . Ells sempre tenen una alternativa ferroviària, però en el nostre cas a l’eix Madrid-Barcelona no la tenim”, ha explicat el director. Recuperar les “línies històriques” La xarxa ferroviària d’alta velocitat es va liberalitzar l’any 2020. Salmerón ha assegurat que va ser una idea que van veure amb bons ulls en un principi, ja que semblava que havia de permetre qualsevol persona poder viatjar amb l’alta velocitat. Ara, però, canvien d’opinió, ja que han vist que no ha existit una alternativa ferroviària econòmica. Salmerón ha assegurat que la solució no és renacionalitzar la xarxa, però sí ha afirmat que “s’ha de canviar la política ferroviària , i això ha de comportar la recuperació de les línies històriques per circular d’una manera més lenta”. stories.headline: Catalan president’s chief of staff resigns amid judicial investigation

sources.body:
Salvador Illa, en una foto de archivo David Zorrakino David Zorrakino / Europa Press

Eduard Rivas , jefe de gabinete del presidente de la Generalitat de Cataluña, Salvador Illa , ha dimitido este lunes del cargo, seis meses después de que se hiciese pública una investigación judicial por presuntas irregularidades en adjudicaciones públicas cuando era alcalde de la localidad barcelonesa de Esparreguera.

Pese a que Illa siempre ha cerrado filas con su mano derecha y a que el propio Rivas sigue defendiendo su inocencia, fuentes consultadas por RTVE esgrimen que ha querido dar un paso atrás para eliminar cualquier sombra de duda sobre el Govern. La Generalitat ha apuntado en un comunicado que el jefe del gabinete renuncia "por decisión propia" y, de hecho, seguirá militando dentro del PSC.

El Govern tiene previsto formalizar este mismo martes el relevo de Rivas y nombrar como remplazo a Xavier Amor, hasta ahora secretario de gobiernos locales y relaciones con el Aran del gobierno catalán.

La investigación judicial se remonta a principios de año y guarda relación con la etapa de Rivas como alcalde de Esparreguera , entre los años 2015 y 2024. Un juzgado de Martorell, Barcelona, examina una batería de contratos municipales vinculado a la Fundación para la Inclusión Laboral (FIL), de la que el exedil era patrón.

Las fuentes consultadas han confirmado que el pasado jueves Rivas tuvo la confirmación de que se levantaba el secreto de sumario del caso, lo que le llevó a presentar su dimisión al día siguiente.

Desde la Generalitat han querido claro que en ningún caso se trata de un cese y, de hecho, en su comunicado Illa agradece "el compromiso y los servicios prestados".

sources.body:
El cap de gabinet de Salvador Illa ha deixat el càrrec arran de la investigació en una causa sobre contractes de la Fundació per a la Inclusió Laboral (FIL) amb l'Ajuntament d'Esparreguera quan ell era l'alcalde.

Els Mossos es van personar a principis d'any a l'Ajuntament per requerir documentació sobre contractes dels serveis de neteja viària i manteniment , en el marc de la investigació per un delicte de malversació de fons públics.

Eduard Rivas va ser l'alcalde d'aquesta població fins que va ser nomenat cap de gabinet de Salvador Illa, l'agost del 2024 . Arran de la dimissió, el substituirà Xavier Amor , el fins ara secretari de Governs Locals i Relacions amb l'Aran, que serà nomenat nou cap de gabinet del president de la Generalitat en el Consell Executiu d'aquest dimarts.

Rivas ha confirmat que dijous passat se li va comunicar que s'havia aixecat el secret de sumari i l'endemà va presentar la renúncia al càrrec.

Assegura que està convençut d'haver actuat "sempre d'acord amb la legalitat" i diu que ha decidit dimitir "seguint els valors d'honor i ètica" i perquè no vol "que hi hagi cap ombra de dubte que pugui interferir en el desenvolupament de la responsabilitat que ocupava fins ara".

"Tanco una etapa de la qual em sento molt honorat i estic molt agraït per la confiança del president Illa. Continuaré treballant al servei de la ciutadania des del PSC ", afegeix.

El ja excap de gabinet d'Illa va ser patró de l'entitat investigada juntament amb quatre alcaldes més de la comarca.

El febrer del 2025, els Mossos d'Esquadra van detenir tres persones –cap d'elles ostentava càrrecs públics– per presumpte desviament de diners públics de la Fundació d'Inserció Laboral (FIL) d'Esparreguera. Part dels diners que rebia la fundació haurien acabat pagant despeses de caràcter privat .

A l'Ajuntament, els Mossos van buscar documentació dels anys 2022, 2023 i 2024 per ordre de la plaça 7 del Tribunal d'Instància de Martorell, que té oberta la causa per un presumpte delicte de malversació de fons públics , segons va informar el Tribunal Superior de Justícia de Catalunya.

A més d'entrar a l'edifici principal de l'Ajuntament, els agents també van buscar informació en altres seus municipals. Segons El Periódico, aquell dia es va intervenir el telèfon mòbil de Rivas , que llavors va demanar personar-se en la causa.

A l'abril, quan es va confirmar que l'investigaven, Illa va ratificar la "confiança plena" en el seu cap de gabinet. En una entrevista a Onda Cero, el cap de l'executiu català va dir que tenia confiança que el cas es resoldria favorablement i va assegurar que era una persona a qui coneixia bé:

En aquests moments li tinc confiança plena. Si tingués evidències, actuaria amb la contundència que correspon en aquests casos.

Illa va valorar que el seu cap de gabinet tenia una actitud correcta de col·laboració amb la justícia i va defensar que no havia amagat res, perquè es tractava d'una investigació secreta.

Llicenciat en Ciències Polítiques, Rivas havia estat assessor de Raimon Obiols i Javi López al Parlament Europeu i va començar la seva carrera com a regidor de Joventut a la seva localitat l'any 2007 .
sources.headline: Plega el cap de gabinet d'Illa, investigat per uns contractes quan era alcalde d'Esparreguera

stories.headline: Two teenagers arrested over alleged role in promoting Barcelona looting

sources.body:
Disturbios en el centro de Barcelona el sábado 24 de octubre / Lorena Sopena / Europa Press

Los Mossos d'Esquadra y la Policía Nacional han detenido, en las comarcas del Maresme y el Bages, a las dos primeras adolescentes arrestadas en España, de 14 y 17 años, por presuntamente coordinar y planificar los disturbios y saqueos registrados en Barcelona el pasado 24 de octubre a través de los canales de comunicación de Blocus.

La investigación de ambos cuerpos policiales han podido comprobar que las detenidas eran administradoras de diferentes grupos de comunicación utilizados para promover las acciones, que se difundieron mediante un cartel publicado en TikTok con un código QR con acceso directo a un canal de WhatsApp. Las pesquisas también han permitido determinar que las detenidas habrían tenido una participación activa en la dinamización del grupo.

Además de las dos chicas, otros dos arrestados por su vinculación con Blocus han entrado en la cárcel en los últimos días.

El último de ellos es un joven de 21 años detenido el sábado en Cabrera d'Anoia (Anoia). Tras tomarle declaración, la magistrada de la Sección de Instrucción del Tribunal de Instancia de Barcelona ha decretado este lunes su ingreso en prisión provisional comunicada y sin fianza. La causa está abierta por desórdenes públicos y organización criminal.

El otro implicado que ha ingresado en prisión es un chico de 18 años de nacionalidad española que fue detenido el viernes en Barcelona como presunto ideólogo de los disturbios de Blocus. Según fuentes policiales, sería uno de los dinamizadores e instigadores de uno de los grupos desde el que se difundían y promocionaban actos delictivos a través de las redes sociales.

Al margen de los ingresos en prisión, la investigación también ha permitido identificar y detener a otras personas relacionadas con Blocus. Entre ellos, el de un menor detenido en Lleida , que quedó en libertad vigilada , y el de otro chico de 17 años arrestado en Sant Sadurní d'Anoia (Alt Penedès), que ha sido internado en un centro de menores.

También en relación con Blocus, la Guardia Civil detuvo en Picanya (Valencia) a un joven de 25 años, de origen paquistaní, considerado presuntamente el creador de Blocus en España y uno de los responsables de los disturbios de Barcelona. El arrestado ha ingresado en prisión provisional.

Por otro lado, otros dos individuos vinculados a Blocus, uno de ellos menor de edad, fueron detenidos por participar activamente en canales de mensajería instantánea en los que se difundían llamamientos a cometer saqueos y actos de pillaje en comercios de Fuengirola y Marbella (Málaga).

Desde el 25 de octubre, 79 menores detenidos han pasado a disposición judicial en los juzgados de menores del Tribunal de Instancia de Barcelona, según ha informado el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Catalunya (TSJC). Los jueces han decretado cinco internamientos en régimen cerrado , 32 libertades vigiladas con prohibición de acudir a manifestaciones y otras 40 libertades vigiladas. Para los dos menores restantes no se ha establecido ninguna medida cautelar.
sources.headline: Detenidas dos menores de 14 y 17 años por planificar y promover los saqueos de Blocus en Barcelona

sources.body:
Els Mossos d'Esquadra i la Policia Nacional, coordinats per la Secció de Menors de la Fiscalia Provincial de Barcelona, han detingut dues noies de 14 i 17 anys al Bages i al Maresme per presumpta relació amb delictes de desordres públics agreujats per pillatge a la ciutat de Barcelona el 24 d'octubre.

A les menors se les acusa de promoure actes violents i saquejos mitjançant els canals de comunicació de Blocus. Segons la policia, eren administradores de diversos grups utilitzats per coordinar les accions, que s'haurien difós mitjançant un cartell publicat a TikTok amb un codi QR d'accés directe a un canal de WhatsApp.

El president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , ha assegurat al seu compte a la xarxa X que les dues noves detencions "demostren que no hi haurà impunitat" i recorda que "qui promogui o participi en aquests fets haurà de respondre davant la justícia".

D'altra banda, aquest dilluns la magistrada de guàrdia de la secció d'instrucció del tribunal d'instància de Barcelona ha decretat presó provisional sense fiança per al detingut de 21 anys de Cabrera d'Anoia per la seva vinculació a Blocus. El noi està acusat de delictes de desordres públics i organització criminal, com a presumpte coordinador dels aldarulls i saquejos violents a Barcelona.

A més, els jutjats de Barcelona han acordat l' internament en règim tancat per a cinc dels menors detinguts pels aldarulls del dissabte 24 d'octubre , que van acabar amb la detenció de 79 joves. Per a la majoria, s'ha acordat llibertat vigilada i alguns també tenen prohibit assistir a manifestacions.

Pel que fa a la investigació dels fets, el ministre d'Exteriors, José Manuel Albares , ha explicat que estan estudiant possibles "ingerències estrangeres" en aquestes convocatòries que s'han fet a través de les xarxes socials sota el nom de Blocus.

stories.headline: Ciutat Vella introduces mobile recycling points to reduce rubbish left on streets

sources.body: Des d’aquest dilluns és més fàcil reciclar en dos barris de Ciutat Vella: el Gòtic i Sant Pere, Santa Caterina i la Ribera . L’Ajuntament de Barcelona hi ha habilitat un total de nou punts de reciclatge mòbils per evitar l’ abandonament de bosses d’escombraries al carrer. Els punts mòbils funcionen de dilluns a dissabte (excepte festius) i ho fan en horari de matí i tarda . Per exemple, a la plaça de Sant Miquel, de 7 h a 9 h i de 13.45 h a 15.45 h. Així doncs, en l’horari indicat, s’habiliten contenidors de tipus bujol (petits amb rodes) per llençar-hi totes les fraccions: plàstic , cartró , vidre , orgànica i residus . També et pot interessar En marxa una prova pilot contra l’incivisme “exagerat” en la neteja a Ciutat Vella Àngels Molina Ester Magdaleno 2 minuts de lectura L’Ajuntament demana un canvi d’hàbit Segons ha detallat aquest dilluns el consistori, els contenidors estaran custodiats en tot moment per personal de neteja, que informarà i orientarà la ciutadania sobre la separació correcta de la brossa. Els contenidors els mouran d’un punt a l’altre amb vehicles elèctrics que han d’arribar al febrer, mentrestant, ho faran amb vehicles tradicionals. Perquè el nou sistema de recollida selectiva arribi a tothom, l’Ajuntament ha imprès fulletons en set idiomes, com ara l’urdú i l’anglès. De fet, un dels objectius del govern municipal és generar un “ canvi d’hàbit ” entre els veïns. “Demanem a la ciutadania que no feia recollida selectiva perquè era difícil, que ara ho faci”, ha dit el director de Serveis de Neteja i Gestió de Residus, Carlos Vázquez . Reciclatge per sota de la mitjana Vázquez també ha demanat a la ciutadania que es “repensi” baixar la brossa al carrer a qualsevol hora i que ho faci dins de l’horari establert. “Més recollida selectiva, menys bosses abandonades a Ciutat Vella”, ha dit. En la mateixa línia, el regidor del districte, Albert Batlle , ha afegit: “Són mesures per millorar la netedat , per facilitar la recollida d’escombraries i incrementar la recollida per fraccions, que ara mateix al barri Gòtic està al voltant del 20 % , mentre que a la resta de la ciutat la mitjana ja se situa cap al 40 % “. El nou servei s’emmarca en la segona fase del Pla de millora de neteja i recollida de residus de Ciutat Vella, que va disposar també d’una prova pilot . Durant la prova, es van reduir les bosses abandonades entre un 30 % i un 42 %, segons l’Ajuntament. Un únic dia de recollida de trastos vells Com a novetat, des d’aquesta tardor cada barri de Ciutat Vella també té assignat un únic dia setmanal per a la recollida de mobles i trastos vells. L’horari és el mateix de sempre, de 20 a 22 h: la Barceloneta: dilluns el Gòtic: dimecres el Raval: dijous Sant Pere, Santa Caterina i la Ribera: divendres També et pot interessar Engega el reglament de la UE per prohibir els envasos monodosi de plàstic d’un sol ús Merche Artacho Vega 3 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: Ciutat Vella habilita punts de reciclatge mòbils per evitar que s’abandoni brossa al carrer

sources.body:
Trabajadores del servicio de limpieza del Ayuntamiento de Barcelona, en una imagen de archivo. / MANU MITRU / EPC

El casco antiguo de la ciudad de Barcelona estrena desde este lunes 2 de noviembre un nuevo servicio de nueve puntos de reciclaje móviles para facilitar la recogida selectiva en Ciutat Vella y reducir el número de bolsas de basura que los vecinos dejan en la calle. La medida está prevista ya desde hace unos meses, dentro del marco del plan de mejora de la limpieza y la recogida selectiva en los barrios del Gòtic y de Sant Pere, Santa Caterina y la Ribera. Concretamente, los vehículos harán parada, mañana y tarde, en nueve puntos del distrito, que constarán de personal que informará a los ciudadanos sobre cómo separar correctamente los residuos.

Los puntos móviles permitirán depositar papel, cartón, vidrio y envases, aunque, de manera "excepcional" , ha advertido el teniente de Alcaldía Albert Batlle, también se permitirá dejar las fracciones 'resto' y orgánica a las personas que "por motivos de edad, movilidad reducida u otras circunstancias tengan dificultades para depositar estos residuos en el horario habitual vespertino", entre las 20 y las 22 horas. "La limpieza es la tercera preocupación en el distrito, tras la inseguridad y el acceso a la vivienda —ha declarado Batlle—. Queremos hacer de Ciutat Vella un espacio que gane en convivencia y en calidad de vida de los vecinos". Además de los informadores, el consistorio ha preparado hojas informativas en siete idiomas diferentes para aumentar la concienciación.

"Es evidente que en el barrio Gòtic faltan puntos de recogida selectiva ", ha asegurado el director del servicio de limpieza y recogida de residuos, Carlos Vázquez, quien ha acompañado a Batlle para explicar las nuevas medidas. Vázquez también ha descrito el horario dispuesto hasta ahora para depositar las fracciones 'resto' y orgánica como "muy exigente" y ha asegurado que "obliga a actuar a la gente con mucho rigor". El consistorio es consciente de que, para funcionar, el nuevo sistema implica un "cambio de hábitos" por parte de la ciudadanía, así como una mayor concienciación : "A los que no hacían recogida selectiva porque era difícil, ya lo puede hacer con facilidad", ha resumido Vázquez. Por su parte, Batlle ha querido realizar un "llamamiento" tanto a la ciudadanía como a los que visitan el barrio para que "incrementen los estándares de civismo".

De hecho, Batlle ha destacado que esta medida ha sido consensuada con la ciudadanía , a quien ha agradecido las reuniones "monográficas" llevadas a cabo con el Ayuntamiento, y de las que surgían los llamados "paseos conjuntos", unas rutas formadas por técnicos municipales y vecinos por los "puntos negros" de la limpieza en el distrito. Del análisis de lo propuesto en esas reuniones se destilan ahora los 42 proyectos y 130 "acciones puntuales" que sustancian la segunda parte del plan . Así, durante este 2026 el Ayuntamiento destaca que se están poniendo en marcha una "batería de mejoras" de entre las que destaca la mejora de la limpieza de las calles del distrito con limpiado mecánico, la limpieza diaria de "puntos críticos de orines" y con alta presión o el incremento de la limpieza de los propios contenedores.
